mainTopic: Liability for becoming טמא inside the עזרה: the source from משכן and מקדש, and the rules of bowing and staying
overview: The משנה says a person who became טמא while already inside the עזרה can be liable. רבי אלעזר learns this from two פסוקים, one saying 'משכן ה׳' and one saying 'מקדש ה׳'. A ברייתא seems to use up both words for other lessons, so the גמרא explains that the lesson comes from the switch between the two names. Since each building can be called by either name, the תורה could have used one word twice. The גמרא then proves from שמות 25:8-9 that the משכן is also called 'מקדש'. Next, רבא explains the משנה's rule about bowing: bowing toward the קודש הקדשים makes a person liable right away, but bowing outward counts only if he stayed long enough to bow. The גמרא defines the long bow as lying fully spread out and measures it by the time it takes to say a פסוק from דברי הימים. A ברייתא then defines קידה, כריעה and השתחוואה. Finally, רבא asks whether this staying is also needed for מלקות, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: became impure inside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה about someone who became טמא while inside the עזרה and then forgot about his טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he became impure in the Temple courtyard and his impurity was hidden from him, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we think of someone who was already טמא and walked into the עזרה. This case is different: he was טהור when he entered and became טמא only once inside. The גמרא will now look for where the תורה teaches liability for this kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש
It was hidden from him, meaning he forgot
And so on: the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: He became impure in the Temple courtyard
and the impurity was hidden from him, etc.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who became טמא inside the עזרה and forgot about it can be liable.

steps.title: Asking for the source for impurity inside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a person is liable for טומאה that happened inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Impurity in the courtyard: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the תורה for the משנה's case of becoming טמא inside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading of the פסוקים talks about someone who comes in already טמא. The גמרא wants a source that also covers someone who became טמא inside and stayed there.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Impurity in the courtyard: from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: He means someone who became impure while already inside, not someone who came in impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק teaching liability for טומאה that happened inside the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר learns it from two verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that one פסוק says 'משכן ה׳ טמא' and another says 'מקדש ה׳ טמא'. Since the second is not needed for טומאה outside, it is applied to טומאה inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: one פסוק says 'He defiled the משכן of ה׳' and another says 'For he defiled the מקדש of ה׳.' If the second is not needed for someone who became impure outside, use it for someone who became impure inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question using a seemingly extra פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים seem to say the same thing. The first already covers someone who became טמא outside and walked in. So the second one is put to use for a new case: someone who became טמא inside.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this matter
Apply it to a different matter

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base source for liability on טומאה that happens inside the עזרה. The rest of the sugya tests whether this source holds up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״אֶת מִשְׁכַּן ה׳ טִמֵּא״,
phrases.english: One verse says: "He has defiled the Tabernacle of the Lord,"

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״כִּי אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ ה׳ טִמֵּא״;
phrases.english: and another verse says: "For he has defiled the Temple of the Lord."
If it is not needed for impurity that happened outside,
apply it to impurity that happened inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second, extra-looking פסוק ('מקדש ה׳ טמא') teaches about טומאה that happened inside the עזרה.

steps.title: Challenge: the verses are not really extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that both פסוקים are actually needed, so neither is free to teach a new lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the verses really extra? They are needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's answer by saying neither פסוק is extra. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's whole answer depends on one פסוק being extra. If each one teaches its own needed lesson, there is no extra פסוק left over to teach about טומאה inside.

phrases.english: But are the verses really extra?!
They are definitely needed!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the second פסוק is extra.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both פסוקים are needed for their own lessons, nothing is left over to teach about טומאה inside the עזרה.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא: each word is needed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting רבי אלעזר himself explains that without 'משכן' we would exclude the משכן, and without 'מקדש' we would exclude the מקדש. So both words are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר says, if 'משכן' is written, why write 'מקדש'? And if 'מקדש' is written, why write 'משכן'? Had it said only 'משכן', I would say he is liable for the משכן, since it was anointed with the anointing oil, but not for the מקדש. Had it said only 'מקדש', I would say he is liable for the מקדש, since its holiness lasts forever, but not for the משכן. That is why it says 'משכן' and that is why it says 'מקדש'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its challenge, showing that each word is needed for its own lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each building has its own special feature. The משכן was anointed with שמן המשחה, and the מקדש has permanent קדושה. Without both words we might think only one of them counts, so both פסוקים are needed. That seems to leave no extra פסוק for רבי אלעזר's lesson.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is also from רבי אלעזר, so the challenge is strong: his own teaching seems to use up both פסוקים.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
If "Tabernacle" is stated, why is "Temple" stated?
And if "Temple" is stated, why is "Tabernacle" stated?
Had it said "Tabernacle" and not "Temple,"

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: עַל מִשְׁכָּן יְהֵא חַיָּיב –
phrases.english: I would have said: he is liable for the Tabernacle,
since it was anointed with the anointing oil,
but he is not liable for the Temple.
And had it said "Temple" and not "Tabernacle,"

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: עַל מִקְדָּשׁ יְהֵא חַיָּיב –
phrases.english: I would have said: he is liable for the Temple,
since its holiness is permanent,
phrases.notes: The משכן's holiness lasted only while it stood; the מקדש's holiness stays forever.

phrases.english: but he is not liable for the Tabernacle.
That is why it says "Tabernacle,"
and that is why it says "Temple."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that both פסוקים are needed and neither is extra.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אלעזר explaining a separate need for 'משכן' and for 'מקדש'.

steps.title: The change in wording teaches two lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's lesson comes from the change in wording. Each building can be called by the other name, so the תורה could have used one word twice. Using two different words teaches both lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what bothered רבי אלעזר: the משכן is called 'מקדש' and the מקדש is called 'משכן'. So let the תורה write 'מקדש' both times or 'משכן' both times! Why use both 'משכן' and 'מקדש'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר by changing where his lesson comes from: it comes from the switch between two words, not from an extra פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each word can mean either building, writing the same word twice would already cover both the משכן and the מקדש. The switch to two different words is the real extra detail. It teaches two lessons: both buildings count, and a person is liable for טומאה that happened inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: The lesson does not come from an extra פסוק. It comes from the תורה choosing two different names, משכן and מקדש, when one name used twice would have been enough.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: This is what was difficult for Rabbi Elazar:
Since the Tabernacle is called "Temple"
and the Temple is called "Tabernacle,"
let it write either "Temple" in both verses,
or "Tabernacle" in both verses!
Why do I need both "Tabernacle" and "Temple"?
Learn two things from it.
phrases.notes: The two lessons: both buildings count, and impurity that happened inside also makes him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocates the source of the lesson from an extra פסוק to a change in wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's lesson depended on a whole פסוק being extra, and the ברייתא shows it is not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since each building can be called by either name, using two different names is extra and teaches two lessons.

steps.title: Where is the Tabernacle called 'Temple'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the מקדש is called 'משכן' (ויקרא 26:11), but asks where the משכן is ever called 'מקדש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the מקדש is called 'משכן', as it says: 'I will place My משכן among you.' But where do we learn that the משכן is called 'מקדש'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one half of the claim from step 6 and asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 6 only works if each name can mean both buildings. One direction has a clear פסוק. The other direction, that the משכן is called 'מקדש', still needs a source.

phrases.english: Granted, the Temple is called "Tabernacle,"
as it is written: "And I will set My Tabernacle among you";
but that the Tabernacle is called "Temple":
from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions an assumption used in the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משכן is also called 'מקדש'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a פסוק calling the משכן 'מקדש', the claim that one word could have covered both buildings is not proven.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the משכן is also called 'מקדש'.

steps.title: First proof rejected: that verse is about the Ark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a proof from 'the קהתים carrying the מקדש' and rejects it, because that פסוק refers to the ארון, not to the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from 'The קהתים, carriers of the מקדש, traveled', that פסוק is written about the ארון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a possible source and then pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קהתים carried the ארון and the holy vessels, not the משכן structure. So the word 'מקדש' there does not show that the משכן itself is called 'מקדש'.

keyTerms.meaning: The family of לוים descended from קהת

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
"And the Kehatites, carriers of the Temple, set forward":
that is written about the Ark!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 7 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only this proposed proof is rejected, not the claim itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that פסוק, 'מקדש' refers to the ארון and holy vessels, not the משכן.

steps.title: The real proof from the building of the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the point from שמות 25:8-9. 'Make Me a מקדש' is followed right away by 'the pattern of the משכן', so the מקדש mentioned there is the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from here: 'Make Me a מקדש and I will dwell among them', and it is written: 'According to all that I show you, the pattern of the משכן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the accepted source that the משכן is called 'מקדש'. This closes the question from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The command to build a 'מקדש' was given in the desert, and the next פסוק calls the same building 'the משכן'. So the משכן is called 'מקדש', and the answer in step 6 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Both names fit both buildings: the מקדש is called 'משכן' (ויקרא 26:11) and the משכן is called 'מקדש' (שמות 25:8-9). That is why the change in wording can teach רבי אלעזר's extra lesson.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from here:
"And let them make Me a Temple, and I will dwell among them,"
and it is written: "According to all that I show you,"
the pattern of the Tabernacle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 8 with a correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In שמות 25:8-9 the building first called 'מקדש' is then called 'משכן', so the משכן is called 'מקדש'.

steps.title: רבא explains that bowing counts only when facing inward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'he bowed, or stayed long enough to bow.' רבא says bowing makes a person liable only when he faces inward. If he faces outward, he is liable only if he stayed long enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He bowed, or he stayed long enough to bow.' רבא said: This was taught only when he bowed facing inward. But if he bowed facing outward, then if he stayed long enough, yes, he is liable. If he did not stay, no, he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to a new line of the משנה, and רבא limits it. Bowing alone makes a person liable only when he faces inward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists bowing as one thing that makes a טמא person liable. רבא says real bowing means facing inward, toward the קודש הקדשים. Bowing outward is not real bowing, so it only counts if he also stayed long enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Staying or lingering for a length of time
Facing inward, toward the קודש הקדשים
Facing outward, away from the קודש הקדשים
'They only taught this when...', a phrase that limits a teaching

phrases.english: [The משנה says:] he bowed, or he stayed long enough to bow.
Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה כְּלַפֵּי פְנִים,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he bowed facing inward,
phrases.notes: 'Inward' means facing toward the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: but if he bowed facing outward,
if he stayed, yes; if he did not stay, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משכן/מקדש discussion to a new line of the משנה about bowing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bowing facing inward makes a person liable. Bowing facing outward makes him liable only if he stayed long enough to bow.

steps.title: Second version: the later clause seems to say bowing itself needs staying
steps.stepSummary: Some place רבא's teaching on the משנה's later words, 'or he stayed long enough to bow.' Those words seem to imply that bowing itself only counts if it includes staying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach רבא's statement on the later clause: 'Or he stayed long enough to bow.' This implies that bowing itself needs staying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's teaching. First it sets up the problem: the משנה's words seem to suggest that bowing always needs staying. This prepares for רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If staying 'long enough to bow' is the measure, then bowing must take time. That would mean a quick bow with no staying never counts. This inference is what רבא responds to.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version)
The later clause of a משנה

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the later clause:
'or he stayed long enough to bow' —
this implies that bowing itself needs staying;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of where רבא's teaching was said.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a simple bow makes a person liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Measuring by 'long enough to bow' suggests that bowing itself always takes time, so a bow with no staying would not count.

steps.title: רבא: the staying requirement applies only to outward bowing
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that bowing needs staying only when facing outward. Facing inward makes him liable even without staying. He then explains how to read the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This was taught only when he bowed facing outward. But facing inward, he is liable even though he did not stay. This is what the משנה means: if he bowed facing inward, or if he stayed long enough to bow while bowing facing outward, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the inference from the last step. Staying matters only when the bowing faces outward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The implication that bowing needs staying is limited to outward bowing. Inward bowing counts by itself. So the משנה's 'or' joins two separate cases: inward bowing, or outward bowing with enough staying.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is what it is saying', which rereads the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions of רבא reach the same practical rule. Inward bowing counts right away, and outward bowing counts only with staying. The difference is which words of the משנה רבא was explaining and what led him to say it.

phrases.english: Rava said: They only taught this
when he bowed facing outward,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כְּלַפֵּי פְנִים – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא שָׁהָה.
phrases.english: but facing inward, [he is liable] even though he did not stay.
And this is what it is saying:
he bowed facing inward,
or he stayed long enough to bow
during that bowing facing outward — he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה כְּלַפֵּי חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference from Step 11 by limiting it to outward bowing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the inference to one case and rereading the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every bow needs staying in order to count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only outward bowing needs staying. Inward bowing counts by itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Facing inward, bowing makes him liable right away. Facing outward, he is liable only if he stayed long enough to bow.

steps.title: What bowing has staying and what bowing has none?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of bowing includes staying and what kind does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a bowing that has staying in it, and what is a bowing that has no staying in it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the two kinds of bowing just mentioned. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule depends on knowing how long a bow takes. So the גמרא needs to define which bowing takes time and which is quick.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
It does not have in it

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה דְּאִית בַּהּ שְׁהִיָּיה,
phrases.english: What is a bowing that has staying in it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵיכִי דָּמֵי הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה דְּלֵית בַּהּ שְׁהִיָּיה?
phrases.english: and what is a bowing that has no staying in it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה דְּאִית בַּהּ שְׁהִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for definitions of the terms used in רבא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the two kinds of bowing differ physically

steps.title: Kneeling has no staying; spreading out hands and feet has staying
steps.stepSummary: Bowing without staying is just kneeling. Bowing with staying is lying flat with hands and feet spread out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bowing with no staying is just kneeling. Bowing with staying is spreading out the hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Plain kneeling is the quick kind of bowing, and lying fully stretched out is the kind that takes time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A quick kneel takes almost no time. Lying fully stretched out, with arms and legs spread, takes longer. That longer bow is the one that sets the measure of 'long enough to bow.'

keyTerms.meaning: Spreading out the hands and feet, lying fully flat

phrases.english: One that has no staying in it —
that is just kneeling;
one that has staying in it —
is spreading out hands and feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלֵית בַּהּ שְׁהִיָּיה – זוֹ כְּרִיעָה בְּעָלְמָא הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Kneeling has no staying. Spreading out hands and feet has staying.

steps.title: How long is the staying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much time counts as 'staying.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is the measure of staying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact length of time. This sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing which bowing takes time is not enough. To know when a person becomes liable, we need the exact amount of time.

phrases.english: And how long is the measure of staying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 14 by asking for the exact length of the longer bow.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of time for 'staying'

steps.title: Two Sages disagree: the whole verse, or from 'and they kneeled' to the end
steps.stepSummary: Two Sages disagree, and there are different versions of who they were. One says the staying is as long as saying a certain whole פסוק. The other says it is as long as saying that פסוק from 'ויכרעו' to the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני and another Sage with him disagree about this; that Sage is רבי שמעון בן פזי. Some say it was רבי שמעון בן פזי and another Sage with him, רבי יצחק בר נחמני. And some say it was רבי שמעון בר נחמני. One said: as long as it takes to say this whole פסוק. The other said: from 'ויכרעו' to the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a disagreement between two Sages. It first records the different versions of their names, then gives the two time measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both Sages measure the staying by how long it takes to say one פסוק. One says the whole פסוק. The other says only the part from 'ויכרעו' to the end, which is shorter. The names are uncertain, but the two opinions are clear.

keyTerms.meaning: One who was with him (another Sage)

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani disagrees about it

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד דְּעִימֵּיהּ, וּמַנּוּ – רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי;
phrases.english: with one who was with him, and who is that? Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi;

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי וְחַד דְּעִימֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: and some say: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi and one who was with him,
and who is that? Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר נַחְמָנִי.
phrases.english: and some say: Rabbi Shimon bar Nachmani.
phrases.notes: So in this version the Sage is רבי שמעון בר נחמני, not רבי יצחק בר נחמני.

phrases.english: One said: as long as it takes to say this verse,
and one said: from 'and they kneeled' to the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי וְחַד דְּעִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15 with a disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the time to say the whole פסוק, or the time to say it from 'ויכרעו' to the end.

steps.title: The verse used to measure the staying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק from דברי הימים that both Sages use as their measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And all the children of Israel saw the fire coming down and the glory of ה׳ upon the House, and they kneeled with their faces to the ground on the floor, and they bowed down and gave thanks to ה׳: for He is good, for His kindness is forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that both Sages were talking about. This lets us see exactly how long each measure is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the people bowing when fire came down on the בית המקדש. One Sage measures by the whole פסוק. The other measures only from 'ויכרעו', where the bowing starts, to the end.
steps.whatToRemember: The longer kind of bowing (fully stretched out) lasts as long as saying דברי הימים ב 7:3, either the whole פסוק or from 'ויכרעו' to the end.

phrases.english: 'And all the children of Israel saw

phrases.aramaic: בְּרֶדֶת הָאֵשׁ וּכְבוֹד ה׳ עַל הַבָּיִת,
phrases.english: the fire coming down, and the glory of God upon the House,
and they kneeled with their faces to the ground on the floor,
and they bowed down and gave thanks to God:
for He is good, for His kindness is forever.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל רֹאִים בְּרֶדֶת הָאֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the פסוק referred to in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure of staying is set by how long it takes to say this פסוק (all of it, or from 'ויכרעו').

steps.title: Three kinds of bowing and their proofs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines קידה as bowing on the face, כריעה as bowing on the knees, and השתחוואה as lying flat with hands and feet spread out. Each definition comes with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: קידה means bowing with the face down, as the פסוק says, 'בת שבע bowed with her face to the ground.' כריעה means bowing on the knees, as the פסוק says, 'from kneeling on his knees.' השתחוואה means spreading out the hands and feet, as the פסוק says, 'Shall I, your mother, and your brothers come to bow down to you to the ground?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains three different Hebrew words for bowing. Each one gets its own picture and its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said the 'staying' with bowing means lying fully flat. This ברייתא backs that up by showing that השתחוואה, the word used there, really means spreading out completely on the ground. The proof is from יעקב's words to יוסף, 'to the ground,' meaning fully stretched out on the earth.

keyTerms.meaning: Bowing with the face toward the ground
Full bowing, lying flat on the ground
Spreading out the hands and feet

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels of bowing: קידה is face down, כריעה is on the knees, and השתחוואה is lying fully flat with arms and legs spread. The 'staying' in the earlier discussion is tied to השתחוואה.
steps.confusionAlert: In everyday speech 'השתחוואה' can mean any bow, but here it has a very specific meaning: lying completely spread out on the ground.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Kidda means bowing on the face,
and so it says:
"Then Bat Sheva bowed with her face to the ground."
Keria means bowing on the knees,
and so it says:
"From kneeling on his knees."
Hishtachava'a: this is spreading out the hands and feet,
and so it says:
"Shall I and your mother indeed come
and your brothers, to bow down to you to the ground?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that defines the bowing terms, supporting the earlier picture of bowing with staying as lying fully flat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידה is on the face, כריעה is on the knees, השתחוואה is spreading out hands and feet, each proven from a פסוק.

steps.title: רבא asks if staying is needed for lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: for a טמא person in the מקדש to get מלקות, does he need to stay there the set amount of time, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: Is staying needed for lashes, or is staying not needed for lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question. We know staying matters for the קרבן, but does it also matter for getting מלקות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the 'staying' was discussed as the condition for bringing a קרבן. רבא wants to know if the same time limit applies to מלקות, or if a warned person is punished right away even without staying that long.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks, raises a question he is unsure about
Staying, remaining for a set amount of time

phrases.english: Rava asked:
Is staying needed for lashes,
or is staying not needed for lashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the idea of staying, which was set for the קרבן, and asks whether it applies to מלקות too.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a warned טמא person needs to stay the set amount of time to get מלקות, or gets it right away.

steps.title: First side: the staying tradition may only be for an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to explain רבא's question: maybe the tradition about staying was only given for a קרבן, not for מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that we have a tradition about staying only for an offering, but we have no tradition about staying for lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying out the first side of רבא's question. The other side comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that staying is needed is a received tradition, and it was learned in connection with the קרבן. So maybe it stays there, and for מלקות a person is punished as soon as he stays at all after being warned.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition, we learned it as a received teaching
An offering brought to the מקדש

phrases.english: For an offering we have a tradition of staying,
but for lashes we have no tradition of staying;

steps.triggerLanguage: לְקׇרְבָּן גְּמִירִי שְׁהִיָּיה, לְמַלְקוּת לָא גְּמִירִי שְׁהִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the first side of רבא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the tradition about staying is limited to the קרבן alone.
